# Sheet

A panel that slides in from an edge and is dragged back to dismiss: the mobile form of a dialog. It stretches when pulled past its edge, its backdrop lightens as it is dragged away, and it springs back on release. It handles focus, Escape, scroll locking, safe areas and the software keyboard.

```tsx
import { Sheet } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/sheet/sheet";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Sheet title="Save to cookbook" trigger={<Button>Save</Button>}>
  <CookbookList />
</Sheet>
<Sheet title="Filters" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} snapPoints={[0.5, 1]}>
  <FilterForm />
</Sheet>
```

## Usage

Use `trigger` for a sheet a button opens, or `open` with `onOpenChange` to control it.

To close the sheet from an action, control it (`open`/`onOpenChange`) and set `open` to `false` in the handler, or wrap each action in `SheetClose` (`import { SheetClose } from "@/components/ouro/sheet/sheet-parts"`, with your components alias): `<SheetClose render={<Button>Copy link</Button>} />`.

It stacks above the page at `--ouro-layer`, a z-index of 50 by default (from ouro-base.css). If your app has fixed bars above z-50, raise it in a `:root` rule of your own after the Ouro tokens, outside any `@layer`: `:root { --ouro-layer: 60; }`. Don't edit the `--ouro-layer: 50` line shadcn wrote; `shadcn add` resets it. Opened from inside a Sheet, it shows above it.

Testing accessibility: in WebKit, Base UI's focus guards take `role="button"` without a name so VoiceOver's cursor stays trapped. Exclude them: `new AxeBuilder({ page }).exclude("[data-base-ui-focus-guard]")`.

## Use instead when

- Use `Dialog` instead when the content should be a centered dialog on larger screens; it renders this sheet on phones.
- Use the page itself (`AuthLayout`) instead for a step the person must take, such as signing in: a person can always put a Sheet away, and Ouro check's `dismissable-step` fails one over a blank page, or over a signed-out page with no way to sign in.

## Props

The props the modes share. Type: `SheetProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The body. It scrolls when it is taller than the sheet. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only, applied to the sheet panel: width and margins (`max-w-lg`, `mx-auto`). Your classes win over Ouro UI's. Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | The label of the sheet's close button: an icon button in the top corner, in view, with a 44px target on a touch screen, as Dialog's is, so a mouse user sees how to close the sheet and a phone's screen reader (which has no Escape key) can always close it. It is the last control in the sheet. Escape and a press on the backdrop close it too. With `hideTitle` the button sits over the body's top corner, so leave that corner clear. |
| `closeOnOutsidePress` | `boolean` | `true` for a modal sheet, `false` with `modal={false}` | Whether a press outside the sheet closes it. With `modal={false}`, `true` makes the panel beside the page close when the person presses the page, so a press on another row both closes it and reaches that row. Focus moving out of it closes it too, by Tab or from your code, so a keyboard closes it as a press does, and focus stays where it went. Menus, popovers and dialogs opened from inside the sheet are part of it, so a press in one of them leaves the sheet open. `false` on a modal sheet keeps it open when its backdrop is pressed. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A short line under the title, read out when the sheet opens. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | The actions row, stacked full width on phones; primary action last. |
| `hideTitle` | `boolean` |  | Hides the title visually. It still names the dialog for screen readers. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the sheet shuts off the rest of the page while it is open. `false` makes it a panel beside a page the person keeps using, such as a live preview of a look: no backdrop, no focus trap and no scroll lock, the page stays at full strength and in reach, and a press or focus on the page leaves the sheet open, unless you pass `closeOnOutsidePress`. Escape, with focus in the sheet, and its close button, shown at its top corner, close it. |
| `scrim` | `boolean` | `false` | With `modal={false}`, lays a layer over the page behind the sheet that paints nothing and passes presses through, so a press on the page still reaches it and, with `closeOnOutsidePress`, closes the sheet. It tints nothing: the page stays in use, and a tint would lower its text's contrast. The sheet's hairline and shadow set it apart. A modal sheet has its backdrop already, so this does nothing there. |
| `side` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"bottom"` | The edge the sheet slides in from and is dragged back to. |
| `snapPoints` | `SheetSnapPoint[]` |  | Heights a bottom or top sheet rests at, smallest first: fractions of the viewport (`0.5`), `px` or `rem`. `snapPoints={[0.5, 1]}` opens at half height and drags up to full. Without snap points the sheet fits its content. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | Names the sheet for screen readers and shows at its top. Always required; hide it with `hideTitle`. |

## Modes

`SheetProps` is a union: pass the props of exactly one mode. Mixing them is a type error.

### Controlled: `SheetControlledProps`

A controlled Sheet: you own `open` and update it in `onOpenChange`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onOpenChange` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called with `false` when the user dismisses the sheet (swipe, Escape, outside press). |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` | Whether the sheet is open. |

Not in this mode (a type error):

- `trigger`: Not with `open`. Remove `open` and `onOpenChange` to let a trigger open the sheet.

### With trigger: `SheetWithTriggerProps`

An uncontrolled Sheet: `trigger` opens it.

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactElement` | The element that opens the sheet, usually a Button: `trigger={<Button>Save</Button>}`. |

Not in this mode (a type error):

- `onOpenChange`: Not with `trigger`. Remove `trigger` to control the sheet with `open` and `onOpenChange`.
- `open`: Not with `trigger`. Remove `trigger` to control the sheet with `open` and `onOpenChange`.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `isOpen`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `open` with `onOpenChange`: `<Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>`.
- `onClose`: Not a prop. `onOpenChange(false)` fires on close: `<Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>`.
- `position`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `side`: `<Sheet side="bottom">`.
- `size`: Not a prop. A sheet fits its content; to set heights use `snapPoints={[0.5, 1]}`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Parts

When these props cannot express your layout, build it from the parts in `@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/sheet/sheet-parts`. See [parts.md](parts.md#sheet-parts) for the required nesting.

## Types

### `SheetSnapPoint`

A snap point for a bottom or top sheet: a fraction of the viewport height (`0.5`), or a height in `px` or `rem` (`"320px"`, `"20rem"`).

```ts
type SheetSnapPoint = number | `${number}px` | `${number}rem`;
```
